source.title: Calibrating Pre-trained Language Classifiers on LLM-generated Noisy Labels via Iterative Refinement
source.authors: Liqing Ye; Agam Shah; Chao Zhang; Sudheer Chava

page_placements.theme: Strong-to-weak and same-size distillation: a student that is smaller than or equal to its teacher sometimes exceeds it

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no garbling or cutoff affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper fine-tunes a pre-trained BERT classifier on LLM-generated labels and compares its clean-test accuracy with the LLM labeler’s accuracy, but it does not use or report Burns et al.’s PGR measure or strong-ceiling comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Burns et al. but does not report their results. Rows record the PLC fine-tuning baseline against the LLM labeler for V1 and the paper’s SiDyP results against PLC for V2. Other denoising baselines and synthetic or real-world non-LLM noise results are not rows because they do not measure these versions’ LLM-label fine-tuning effects.
record.test_reason: A noisy-label learning paper, not a weak-to-strong test. The 'supervisors' are large LLMs (Llama-3-70b/405b, GPT-4o, Mixtral-8x22b). The student is a much smaller BERT classifier. The student is weaker than the labeler, so no row measures a strong model trained on a weaker model's labels. Burns et al. is cited only as related work on LLM annotation. There is no PGR, no strong ceiling and no weak/strong size manipulation. SiDyP is a denoising method for a small student, not a weak-to-strong training change.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SiDyP improves BERT classifiers trained on LLM-generated noisy labels (about 7.2–7.3% average gains) across tasks, LLMs and prompting styles. They make no claim about weak-to-strong generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fine-tunes a pre-trained BERT classifier using LLM-generated labels and compares the classifier with the labeler, but uses accuracy rather than PGR and does not report a strong-model ceiling. SiDyP additionally refines candidate labels with a diffusion model.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dataset, LLM supervisor, and zero-shot versus few-shot prompting; PLC exceeds the supervisor in some conditions and falls below it in others.

fits_no_version.finding: A small BERT classifier fine-tuned on large-LLM labels sometimes exceeds the labeler's raw test accuracy, by up to about 7.6 points (SemEval, Llama-3.1-70b zero-shot). In other cases it falls below (TREC few-shot 77.72 vs 84.00; 20News 71.2 vs 74.04). The SiDyP denoising method raises the student further, above the labeler in every reported condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Strong-to-weak label distillation: a smaller student trained on a larger LLM's noisy labels can exceed the labeler's accuracy on the task, depending on task and noise structure.

record.peer_reviewed: KDD ’25, Proceedings of the 31st ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
record.problems: The study does not report PGR or a strong-model ceiling. Raw LLM accuracy has no uncertainty value reported alongside the PLC standard deviations. The PLC comparison with the LLM supervisor is mixed across tasks and prompting conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant V1/V2 rows left out. Other noisy-label methods in Tables 1 and 3 are not included because they are neither the naive PLC weak-label fine-tuning baseline nor the SiDyP-versus-PLC training-change comparison.
record.verdict_notes: The record mislabels the relation as 'tests'/T2. The supervisor-student size relation is inverted relative to Burns et al., so V1/V2 do not apply. Data oddity: Table 7 'noise ratio' values (e.g. NumClaim zero-shot 91.69) track LLM accuracy, not error rate, so the label appears mislabeled. Raw LLM accuracies carry no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The paper compares fine-tuned PLC accuracy with raw LLM accuracy but does not compute PGR or report a strong-model ceiling; it does not establish that the LLM is weaker in general.
Tests SiDyP label refinement against naive PLC fine-tuning, not auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, or loss variants; it does not calculate PGR.

relation.reason: Burns et al. is cited as reference [7] in the introduction's discussion of label reliability; weak-to-strong generalization is neither tested nor used as a finding.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates denoising predictions from BERT classifiers trained on large-LLM labels. It does not establish a stronger student learning from a weaker supervisor, report PGR, or test another claim version.

source_check.notes: The 7.6-point maximum concerns plain PLC fine-tuning, not SiDyP. Results use clean test sets, noisy validation for model selection, and mean ± standard deviation across five seeds; model size alone does not establish the capability ordering asserted in the pack.
